title: Design Guardianship: Contribution Runway, RFC Intake, and Sunset Flow
creator: Lena Chen
description: Establish an operational 'guardianship' process for the design system that standardizes how designers and engineers contribute tokens and components, how RFCs are triaged and approved, and how features/components are gracefully sunsetted. This ticket produces: contribution runway docs, an RFC intake template and triage flow, a lightweight review checklist for token/prop changes, a deprecation (sunset) playbook, and automation hooks for registry updates and migration notices.
acceptance_criteria: A single contribution guideline doc that covers token changes, component API changes, and chart config changes
An RFC template populated in the Design Confluence space and a defined triage cadence for RFCs
A 12-item review checklist used by design+engineering reviewers and added to PR templates
A documented sunset flow that includes compatibility matrix requirements, migration guidance, and communications templates
Automation proof-of-concept that posts migration notes to the changelog and opens a design review task when token rename is detected
tasks: Draft Contribution Runway (tokens, components, charts) — include naming, aliasing, and migration patterns
Create RFC intake template and add to Confluence + link in PR template
Design review checklist: accessibility, token usage, backward-compat, visual regression steps
Draft Sunset Flow with timelines, owner roles, and billing/usage considerations for Dedicated customers
Prototype a GitHub Action that detects token key changes and comments on PR with migration hints
Coordinate with ENG on automated registry updates and deprecation flags
Run tabletop with PM and Support to validate customer communication templates
Publish final docs and announce in #design and product-all channels
review_checklist: Accessibility: keyboard, contrast, focus order validated
Token semantics: new token names documented and aliases provided
Backward compatibility: prop defaults preserved or migration path provided
Visual regression: storybook/phantom or Percy checks included
Performance: table/chart renders checked for large datasets
API surface: public props documented and versioned
Docs: migration guide, code examples, and changelog entry prepared
Testing: unit + integration tests added where applicable
Release signals: feature flagging, rollout plan, and fallback strategy
Security/Privacy: any data-path changes reviewed with Security
migration_plan: Identify impacted consumers via registry and usage query (design-tokens + UI components)
Provide alias tokens for one release cycle and mark original deprecated
Publish migration guide with codemods for common repos
Open a cross-team migration tracker and weekly sync for high-impact changes
After 2 releases, remove deprecated keys and notify via changelog + direct emails to affected teams

notes: Trade-offs: shorter deprecation windows speed cleanup but increase migration burden; chosen 2-release window balances cleanup and stability.
We aim to keep public component props stable; breaking changes require RFC and a migration path.
Design tokens should favor clear semantic names (eg. surface-bg, surface-border) over raw color names to reduce churn.
Tie sunset decisions to usage metrics — low-usage components with high maintenance cost are prime candidates.
Consider adding a 'compatibility badge' for components with stable APIs for at least 6 months
